title: National highway network length
definition: Total length of roads designated as National Highways by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways.
notes: Network length grows partly by building new roads and partly by re-designating existing state highways as national highways. The two are not distinguished in the headline figure, so this series overstates new construction.
Use 'National highways constructed per year' alongside this for the build-rate picture.

title: National highways constructed per year
definition: Kilometres of national highway completed during the fiscal year.
notes: The honest read: construction peaked at 13,327 km in FY2020-21 and has since plateaued around 10,000-12,000 km a year. The 'record pace' framing does not survive contact with this series.
FY2020-21's peak coincided with pandemic-period low traffic, which eased construction windows.

title: Access-controlled high-speed corridors and expressways
definition: Length of access-controlled national high-speed corridors and expressways — the grade-separated, limited-access subset of the network.
notes: This is the most genuinely impressive infrastructure series on the site: a 55-fold increase off a near-zero base in a decade.
Still small in absolute terms — China's expressway network is roughly thirty times longer.

title: Four-lane and above national highways
definition: Length of national highway with four or more lanes.
notes: Lane-width upgrades matter more for freight throughput than raw network length. This series has grown faster than total network length, which is the right direction.

title: Operational airports
definition: Count of airports and airstrips in India handling scheduled commercial passenger flights.
notes: Counts drift between releases (157, 159, 160, 163) because 'operational' sometimes includes heliports, water aerodromes and seasonally-served strips. Treat the trend as solid and any single year as ±5.
Several UDAN airports have since lost their scheduled service. An airport being built is not the same as an airport being used — see the route-viability caveats on the methodology page.

title: Airports by classification
definition: Breakdown of operational airports by customs and international designation.

title: Aerodromes operationalised under UDAN
definition: Count of airports, heliports and water aerodromes brought into scheduled service under the UDAN regional connectivity scheme since 2016.

title: UDAN routes inaugurated
definition: Cumulative count of regional air routes started under the UDAN scheme.
notes: Cumulative inaugurations, not currently-flying routes. A material share of UDAN routes have been discontinued after their three-year viability-gap subsidy expired — the scheme's central unresolved weakness.

title: Operational metro rail network
definition: Total length of metro rail in revenue service across Indian cities.
notes: India passed 1,000 km in October 2025 to become the third-largest metro network in the world, behind China and the United States.
Ridership has not kept pace with track: several networks run far below the projections used to justify them. Length is an input, not an outcome.

title: Cities with operational metro rail
definition: Count of Indian cities with a metro system in revenue service.

title: Daily metro rail ridership
definition: Average daily passenger journeys across all operational Indian metro systems.
notes: Ridership grew 4x while network length grew 4.1x — meaning average passengers per kilometre has been flat. New lines are not, on average, as well used as the old ones.

points.note: Fiscal year 2013-14, aligned to the 2014 network-length observation.

title: Cargo handled at major ports
definition: Total cargo throughput at India's centrally-administered major ports in a fiscal year.

title: Cargo handled at all ports
definition: Total cargo throughput across both major and non-major (state) ports.
notes: Non-major ports have grown faster than major ports over the period, driven largely by private terminals on the west coast.

title: Total port capacity
definition: Installed annual cargo handling capacity across major and non-major ports.
notes: Capacity (2,817 MTPA) runs well ahead of throughput (1,668 MT) — utilisation near 59%. Headroom is healthy; it also means further capacity spending has weak near-term returns.

title: Average vessel turnaround time at major ports
definition: Mean time a vessel spends in port from arrival to departure.
notes: Genuine operational gain, and one of the few Indian logistics metrics that now beats several developed-economy averages.
Turnaround improvement has stalled since FY2021-22 — from 52.87 to 48.84 hours in four years, against a halving in the decade before.
